Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (provisionally applied; investment provisions requiring ratification remain subject to applicable implementation status)
Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (in force; investment chapter applies subject to its scope and reservations)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, including terrorist-property provisions; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), S.C. 2017, c. 21; Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, Part XVIII, for individuals with significant control records of federal corporations. There is no single federal UBO register or federal decree governing limited partnerships. Partnership beneficial-ownership and registration requirements are determined principally by the applicable province or territory. For federal corporations, an individual with significant control generally includes a person owning or controlling 25% or more of voting rights or fair-market-value equity, or exercising control in fact, under CBCA ss. 2.1 and 21.1-21.303.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Apply a documented risk-based AML/CFT program consistent with the PCMLTFA and applicable FINTRAC regulations. Identify and verify every natural person exercising ownership or control, including indirect ownership, control in fact, settlors, trustees, beneficiaries, protectors, and controlling general partners where applicable. Screen partners, UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, counterparties, and payment beneficiaries against United Nations sanctions, Canadian consolidated sanctions lists and regulations, Canadian terrorist-property prohibitions, Special Economic Measures Act measures, Magnitsky sanctions, and relevant foreign lists including OFAC SDN and related lists. OFAC screening is not universally mandatory for a Canadian LP but is required or commercially necessary where there is a US nexus, US financial institution, US person, US-dollar clearing, or contractual requirement. Determine domestic and foreign PEP, head-of-international-organization, and family/close-associate status; apply enhanced measures, senior approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and enhanced ongoing monitoring where required. Escalate sanctions or PEP matches for false-positive resolution before onboarding and prohibit transactions involving designated persons or property.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: No single federal company-registry portal is available for forming a Canadian limited partnership. Name searches, reservations, and partnership registrations are filed through the applicable provincial or territorial registry, such as Ontario Business Registry, British Columbia Corporate Online, Alberta Corporate Registry, Quebec Registraire des entreprises, or the equivalent registry in the selected province or territory. Corporations Canada is not the ordinary formation registry for a provincial limited partnership.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The governing province or territory controls partnership-name rules. Names generally must be distinctive, not confusing with existing registrations, and not misleading as to legal form, business, government affiliation, or regulated activity. Quebec filings and public-facing business names are subject to Quebec language requirements, principally the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, including applicable French-language disclosure and naming obligations. English, French, or bilingual names may be accepted elsewhere, subject to local registry rules. Transliteration is generally permitted for a trade name only where the registry accepts it and the resulting name is not confusing, prohibited, or misleading. A limited partnership should use an accepted legal-form designator such as Limited Partnership, L.P., or the locally prescribed equivalent.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying a regulated financial, insurance, securities, health, educational, charitable, or governmental function
Any name that is identical or confusingly similar to an existing corporate or partnership name, trademark, or protected business name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Because no federal LP name-reservation regime exists, confirm the rule of the selected provincial or territorial registry. Where a reservation is available, file the registry-prescribed name search or reservation application, pay the applicable fee, and complete registration before the stated reservation expiry, commonly 30 days but not uniform across Canada. A reservation is not a guarantee of final registration. On rejection, obtain the written reason or deficiency notice, correct distinctiveness, legal-form, language, consent, or sensitive-word issues, and resubmit within the registry deadline. If the registry provides an internal reconsideration or appeal process, file the prescribed request with supporting evidence, including consent letters, trademark evidence, corporate-group information, and proof that the name is not confusing. Exhaust the applicable administrative process before seeking judicial review under the governing provincial or territorial judicial-review statute. There is no general federal administrative appeal for a provincial or territorial LP name rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A limited partnership must maintain the registered office, records, service address, or local address required by the governing provincial or territorial partnership statute and registry. A commercial virtual office may be accepted for registry and service purposes if it provides a valid physical Canadian address, reliable document receipt, and access to required records, but a mailbox-only address is generally inadequate. For digital webtoon publishing and multilingual chapter-unlocking activities, no general federal sector licence is ordinarily required; however, payment processors, Apple, Google, banks, tax authorities, and AML-regulated service providers may require evidence of real management, operational personnel, publishing rights, contracts, accounting records, and transaction activity. A virtual office does not by itself establish tax residence, permanent establishment, commercial substance, or eligibility for treaty benefits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection is low, approximately 1%-3%, for a low-risk digital publishing LP with complete filings, ordinary payment flows, and no complaints or regulatory triggers. The estimate is not a statutory probability and is not predictive. The risk may increase materially following AML alerts, sanctions concerns, unexplained payment flows, tax anomalies, consumer complaints, copyright complaints, suspected misrepresentation, licensing concerns, or inability to contact the partnership at its registered address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act (provincial enactment; e.g., R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16, ss. 2-5 for Ontario); federal taxation characterization under Income Tax Act, R.S.C., 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), s. 96 (partnership pass-through). Note: The Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) does not provide for limited partnerships; formation is effected at the provincial Registry, with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Number constituting the mandatory federal registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Provincial Registry for the LP's formation (e.g., Ontario Business Registry, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch); federal nexus via CRA Business Registration Online; Corporations Canada is not the filing authority for limited partnerships.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 3 Declaration under the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act (or equivalent provincial LP registration form) filed electronically via the Ontario Business Registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Canadian limited partnership; capital contributions are fixed contractually in the Limited Partnership Agreement, may be cash, property or services, and are not subject to any escrow or deposit requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner adopts the Limited Partnership Agreement dated [DATE], together with the attached schedule of initial Limited Partners and capital contributions; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Partnership be established at [ADDRESS], Province of Ontario, Canada, and that the prescribed Limited Partnership Declaration be executed and filed with the provincial Registry; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [NAME] be and is hereby appointed initial manager and signing officer with full authority to apply for the federal Business Number with the Canada Revenue Agency, open banking accounts, execute the partnership's publishing agreements, and effect all ancillary filings; all as determined necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry (Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery) or equivalent provincial registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request through the provincial registry portal for the proposed partnership name; confirm the name is distinct and includes the statutory designation 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.'; where the portal permits, reserve the approved name for the prescribed statutory period (usually 90 days).
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report
Proposed limited partnership name
Identity document and contact details of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for distinctiveness or prohibited wording, file a written rebuttal with the registrar or select an amended name and re-run the NUANS search.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement and capital subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Not applicable – private contractual document executed among the general partner and limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a Limited Partnership Agreement defining capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, management authority of the general partner, transfer and withdrawal restrictions, indemnification and dissolution mechanics; obtain signature counterparts from all partners and record capital subscriptions.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement
Capital subscription schedules
Identity and address verification documents for each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any term is incomplete or contested, amend the agreement by unanimous written consent of all partners prior to any filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration with the provincial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry – Companies and Personal Property Security Branch, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 3 Declaration online setting out the partnership name, registered office address, full legal name and address of the general partner, the statement that the general partner is a limited partnership or corporation (as applicable), and a description of the business activity (ISIC 9000 / NAICS 511130 digital webtoon publishing); pay the prescribed fee electronically.
required_dossiers: Form 3 Declaration (online-generated)
General partner's name and Ontario address for service
Registered office address within Ontario
Business activity description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Declaration is queried for defect (e.g., missing address or non-compliant name), correct the record in the Ontario Business Registry or refile the amended Declaration; registry fees are non-refundable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal CRA Business Number and program account registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership for a federal Business Number (BN) using the CRA Business Registration Online portal; select the 'Partnership' entity type; open program accounts as applicable, including GST/HST (mandatory once taxable revenues exceed CAD 30,000 or voluntarily), payroll (if employees are hired) and import/export (if a non-resident licensing structure is used); the general partner acts as the CRA contact person.
required_dossiers: Provincial LP registration certificate or completed Declaration
Limited Partnership Agreement
General partner's identification (SIN or corporation identifier)
Partnership bank account details (optional at this stage)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA requests clarification or supporting documentation, provide certified copies of the LP Declaration and a general partner resolution through Business Registration Online or the CRA business enquiries service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Extra-provincial registration (where carried on outside registration province)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial registries of the extracprovincial jurisdiction (e.g., British Columbia Corporate Online, Alberta Corporate Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the LP will carry on business in a province other than the province of registration, file an extra-provincial registration in each such province; Canada has no single federal LP register, so provincial reciprocity is required to legalize extra-provincial operations.
required_dossiers: Original provincial LP registration certificate
Certificate of status from the home province
Registered office address in the extra-provincial jurisdiction
General partner's authorization resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing penalties accrue from the date of commencing business; cure by expedited filing with payment of the prescribed late fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-formation corporate governance and banking onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner (internal governance); financial institution (bank account opening)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first meeting of the general partner; adopt the First Resolution of the General Partner confirming the Limited Partnership Agreement, registered office and officer appointments; open the partnership operating account presenting the resolution, LP registration certificate and KYC documents; set up the internal minute book and register of partners.
required_dossiers: First Resolution of the General Partner
Provincial LP registration certificate
Partnership minute book and partner register
Capital contribution receipts and banking KYC forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the financial institution requires enhanced due diligence, provide certified true copies of the LP Agreement, registry search results and underlying IP licensing agreements for the webtoon catalog.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sectoral industrial licensing authority applies to ISIC 9000 / NAICS 511130 digital webtoon publishing; the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) does not license non-broadcast digital content. General regulatory oversight is exercised by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) for digital services, and municipal licensing authorities for any physical office premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no federal, provincial or municipal operating permit is statutorily required for webtoon digital publishing; the LP must remain compliant with private-law contractual requirements of Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, and with the PIPEDA privacy regime for personal data of readers.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) and Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – registration not required; the activity is office-based digital publishing with no prescribed industrial activity under the Ontario Environmental Activity and Sector Registry (EASR) or the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act list of designated projects; no full EIA report or environmental compliance approval is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: De minimis environmental footprint: office wastewater discharged to municipal sewer must comply with the local sewer-use by-law; no process wastewater, VOC emissions or hazardous air pollutants arise from server-side publishing operations; discarded electronic equipment must be disposed of in accordance with Ontario Regulation 103/94 (waste electrical and electronic equipment) where office hardware is retired.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the leased office premises, obtain a fire safety inspection and fire safety plan approval under the Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07), maintain annual certification of fire alarms and extinguishers, secure a building occupancy permit in accordance with the Ontario Building Code, and comply with the general duty provisions of the Occupational Health and Safety Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. O.1, s. 25; workplace accessibility obligations under the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005 also apply to the physical workplace.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC), with the principal business portal 'My Business Account' (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/services/business.html), supplemented by GST/HST NETFILE and 'Represent a Client' for authorized representatives.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident limited partnership carrying on business in Canada must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) by filing Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number' via the CRA online business registration tool or mailed application. The BN is the statutory base; a GST/HST program account (prefix RT) is added where taxable supplies exceed the registration threshold, while an income tax program account (RC) is opened if the LP has Canadian-source income and no other CRA account. For a foreign LP without a Canadian physical address, the non-resident must appoint a fiscal representative acceptable to the CRA under subsection 273(1) of the Excise Tax Act (ETA) for GST/HST purposes, and must execute the CRA 'Non-Resident Business Number Registration' procedures, proving the authority of a Canadian general partner or fiscal agent. Identity verification is conducted through the Canadian resident partner's CRA credential or via a notarized Form RC1A and proof of partnership registration in the foreign jurisdiction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; a limited partnership is fiscally transparent by default under section 96 of the Income Tax Act (ITA), under which income is computed at the partnership level and allocated to each partner. Key statutory elections applicable in this structure include: (i) ITA subsection 96(3) election respecting a deemed partnership year-end and the continuation of the partnership on admission of new partners; (ii) ITA subsection 143.2(1) election to re-characterize a substituted partnership interest on the admission of a new partner; (iii) ETA subsection 156(1) election to treat a supply between closely related persons (corporations or partnerships) as not being a taxable supply, where the LP and a Canadian operating affiliate satisfy the close-relationship tests; (iv) ETA subsection 273(1) election/designation of a fiscal resident representative for the non-resident LP; and (v) elections respecting the GST/HST quick method of accounting. There is no elective commodity-tax hybrid mismatch election; the mandatory hybrid mismatch rules introduced by the 2023 Federal Budget (ITA subsection 96(5.1) and section 247.1) neutralize certain deductible-imbalance outcomes without elective action.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) imposed under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (ETA) and administered federally as a destination-based consumption tax. In Ontario, the harmonized rate is 13%; Quebec applies QST at 9.5% on top of the 5% GST (combined 14.975%), while Saskatchewan, Manitoba, and British Columbia levy separate provincial sales taxes (PST) without harmonization. Digital webtoon sales to Canadian end-users through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing are subject to the HST applicable in the recipient's province, generally collected by the digital platform under the marketplace deemed-supplier rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000, being the threshold of worldwide taxable supplies (excluding GST/HST zero-rated supplies) measured over any preceding four consecutive calendar quarters under ETA subsection 148(1). For the webtoon syndication model, zero-rated digital supplies to non-resident readers do not count toward the threshold, but digital supplies made to Canadian consumers through Apple/Google marketplace platforms are attributed by the deemed-supplier regime (ETA subsection 242.1(2)), and the licensed platforms themselves cross the CAD 30,000 threshold and collect the applicable HST at checkout.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time e-invoice clearance (CTC) system, no fiscal stamping, and no API-based real-time fiscal reporting to CRA. E-invoicing is voluntary, with the Canadian Digital Service (CDS) and PEPPOL BIS 3.0 as accepted interoperability standards for B2B electronic exchange. GST/HST returns are filed electronically via GST/HST NETFILE or certified third-party software, on a monthly/quarterly/annual basis depending on taxable supply volume. Statutory invoicing content is prescribed by ETA subsection 223(1) and must show the supplier's BN and program account, the date of supply, the tax rate, and the net tax payable; for zero-rated exports, invoices must be annotated with a zero-rating mechanism. Apple IAP and Google Play Billing act as deemed suppliers/collectors for domestic Canadian supplies, and the LP must retain the platforms' gross-revenue statements, tax remittance files, and settlement reports as complete fiscal records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for digital webtoon exports is available under ETA Schedule VI section 23, which zero-rates a supply of intangible personal property (including a digital product) made to a non-resident recipient where the recipient is not resident in Canada, is not registered for GST/HST, and the supply is not 'received in Canada'; alternative relief may arise under Schedule VI section 13 for services exported to non-residents. The supplier must maintain reliable transaction-based place-of-supply evidence, including IP geolocation, billing country, storefront country, and Apple/Google subscriber data, showing delivery into the foreign jurisdiction. There is no customs export declaration requirement for electronically delivered intangibles; the digital delivery and settlement trail constitutes the export evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / N/A for intangible electronic services, replaced by the platform's digital delivery logs and the LP's geolocated distribution record
Bill of Lading / N/A for digital goods, substituted by the Apple IAP and Google Play Billing weekly/monthly sales extraction reports evidencing the non-Canadian storefront territories
Webtoon syndication and reseller agreements with each non-resident digital distributor, evidencing that title, delivery, and control of the digital content occur outside Canada
Zero-rated tax invoices meeting ETA section 223 invoice content requirements, annotated with the applicable Schedule VI zero-rating provision

Inward Remittance Certificate / FX settlement reports from Apple and Google generated in settlement currency, reconciled monthly to CAD using CRA-acceptable exchange rates (Bank of Canada noon rates or CRA-approvable methodologies)
General ledger export reconciliation and retained e-audit files demonstrating the exclusion of zero-rated export turnover from the Canadian HST base
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audit scrutiny of export zero-rating concentrates on place-of-supply documentation, the non-resident status of the recipient, and platform integrity. False or fraudulent zero-rating, or arrangements that mischaracterize Canadian-dimensioned digital sales as foreign exports, trigger: (i) reassessment beyond the normal four-year window under ETA subsection 298(3) for misrepresentation committed with gross negligence or wilful default (extended seven-year window); (ii) the 25% penalty imposed by ETA subsection 285(1) on the fraudulent tax amount; (iii) daily compounding interest under ETA subsection 280(1) at the CRA-prescribed rate plus a provincial supplementary rate; (iv) prosecution and fines under ETA section 327.1 and Income Tax Act section 239, reaching CAD 1,000,000 on indictment and up to five years' imprisonment for officers/partners; (v) joint and several liability of all Canadian and non-resident partners under ETA subsection 272.1(1); and (vi) retroactive HST clawback on every previously zero-rated sale, causing irrecoverable consumer-borne HST because end-user invoices cannot be reissued after the fact, plus potential cancellation of the LP's GST/HST registration and BN.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BOC) as the monetary authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as the federal banking prudential regulator; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as the financial intelligence unit; Department of Finance Canada as the policy lead for foreign exchange and payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains fully liberalized capital and current account convertibility. The Canadian dollar (CAD) is a freely floating currency with no exchange control legislation, no prior approval requirements for cross-border remittances, and no restrictions on dividend or profit repatriation to non-resident partners. Remittances are subject to Part XIII withholding tax (generally 25%, reduced by treaty) and to normal anti-money-laundering reporting thresholds. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment, are permitted without currency conversion approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose any mandatory surrender, repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio for export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency bank accounts in Canada or offshore. The only compliance obligations relate to accurate bookkeeping, tax reporting of foreign-source income, and mandatory reporting of cross-border transfers exceeding CAD 10,000 under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility for wholly digital cross-border financial technology EMI providers (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Stripe Treasury) as primary banking rails. Such entities are not banks in Canada and cannot hold 'deposits' without a license; they typically operate as payment service providers or as agents of regulated Canadian banks. Legal constraints under the Bank Act and the PCMLTFA require MSB registration with FINTRAC and, for certain activities, provincial money-services licensing. An LP may use these rails for payment disbursement, but the capital escrow account must reside at a scheduled bank or an authorized foreign bank branch with OSFI approval. Full treasury duties, including FX execution, should be centralized at a tier-1 Canadian bank for cost efficiency and settlement certainty.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is not an absolute statutory mandate under Canadian federal law. Each Schedule I bank sets its own AML/KYC policy. Remote onboarding with live video verification, notarized corporate documents, and digital signature is generally accepted for domestic and non-resident limited partnerships. However, for the general partner and any legal counsel, most large banks require a live video conference with the authorized signatory and the ultimate beneficial owner of the cyber-entity, plus notarized/original certified copies of the LP agreement and partnership registration. In practice, a physical presence at a Canadian branch or at a Canadian embassy/consulate (for notarization) may be requested to satisfy enhanced due diligence for higher-risk jurisdictions; for the stated low-risk digital webtoon publishing business, remote opening is viable with the availability of a Canadian registered office address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership transparency for a multi-tiered limited partnership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/KYC dossier consisting of: (1) the full updated LP agreement with a current schedule of partners, capital contributions, and allocation percentages; (2) an organizational chart tracing all partners to natural persons or verified entities; (3) beneficial ownership declarations for each partner holding 25% or more of the partnership; (4) certified copies of the passports or national IDs of the general partner and all UBOs; (5) CRS/FATCA classification forms; and (6) a legal opinion from Canadian counsel confirming the partnership is not a tax-transparent shell and is engaged in substantive digital publishing operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for cross-border capital injection from digital content licensing revenues
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) audited or internally consistent financial statements for the preceding 12 months; (2) executed platform revenue-sharing agreements with Apple, Google, and comic distribution counterparties; (3) bank statements from the funding bank showing the origin of monies collected; (4) invoice-license logs matching webtoon syndication contract numbers; and (5) an explanation memorandum confirming that funds derive from legitimate digital sales, net of applicable sales-related platform fees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident general partner raising jurisdictional nexus red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The relationship should be articulated as an Ontario-certified or federal extra-provincial registered limited partnership with a Canadian registered agent and a physical operations address. Provide (1) certificate of extra-provincial registration; (2) a completed bank-specific beneficial ownership schedule; (3) a director/general partner declaration confirming authorized signatories; and (4) a tax structure declaration showing the LP is exclusively engaged in the business of digital webtoon publishing/syndication with a substantive Canadian presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intellectual property and royalty flow ambiguity relative to the commodity/export character
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) a description of the Canadian copyright ownership structure, including registration certificates under the Canadian Copyright Act; (2) a detailed royalty flow chart showing consideration for licensed digital content is paid to the LP; (3) written confirmations from platform payment processors (Apple and Google) identifying the LP as the beneficial merchant; and (4) a tax opinion letter confirming no export of physical goods and that payments are royalties, not trading proceeds subject to special tax provisions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital must be transferred via SWIFT MT103 using the partnership's CAD operating or escrow account. Purpose code must be classified as 'Capital contributions' under the Canadian Balance of Payments reporting framework (or bank-specific code for direct investment/equity). No separate exchange-control approval is required. The following protocol applies: (a) the remitting bank must use the exact legal name as registered on the Canadian LP certificate, including the GP's name; (b) the LP's full address and the Canadian bank account number (5/7/12 digit format) must be accurately stated; (c) accompanying memo should reference the definitive LP agreement and partnership capital call; (d) if the transfer exceeds CAD 10,000, the remitter must complete the standard financial institution inquiry; (e) for amounts exceeding CAD 1 million, the bank may request a capital call notice and a board/GP resolution authorizing the injection. No exchange conversion is required if monies are held in USD; conversion to CAD may be executed at the LP's discretion on the local account without reporting to the central bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements (license payments to content creators, translators, and rights holders) will be cleared through: (a) SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers to non-Canadian payees, using 'Business/presentment' purpose code (e.g., '7210 - Rights to books, manuscripts and other informational content' or a code suggested by the payee's bank); (b) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) may be used for larger contracts requiring documentary compliance; however, for digital content the normative rail is wire transfer. Direct disbursements to individuals should follow the EFT protocol for payroll/contractors, while payments to corporate counterparts should use ACH via the Canadian domestic clearing system (Quebec-ACH or LVTS) for CAD payments, and the Clearing House Interbank Payments System (CHIPS) or SWIFT for USD cross-border disbursements. Each payment invoice must include a cross-reference to the specific chapter-unlocking sales report to support the transaction description for AML review, but no statutory FX approval is required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts (plain-vanilla deliverable forwards) with a Canadian Schedule I bank or authorized derivatives dealer, permitted only for hedging the LP's known USD/CAD receipt exposures derived from Google and Apple revenue flows; physical delivery of CAD is customary on maturity.

FX swaps (currency swaps) executed bilaterally with an OSFI-regulated Canadian bank under an ISDA master agreement, subject to mandatory central clearing and trade-reporting requirements if the LP exceeds applicable derivatives transaction thresholds (typically derivatives net notional > CAD 5 billion).

NDFs (Non-Deliverable Forwards) are not applicable in the CAD/USD relationship because the CAD is freely deliverable; they would be non-permissible for speculative intent and would offer no compliance advantage.

Options on USD/CAD (call and put) may be used for risk-management purchases covering revenue shortfall scenarios, provided the option underlying is a physical FX transaction on the LP's account and the instrument is booked with a Canadian financial institution.

Cross-currency swaps are allowed for long-term currency liability management, but must be limited to genuine economic hedges of revenue streams under the digital content licensing agreements; speculative hedging is restricted by OSFI guidance and the partnership's investment mandate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to CAD 500 per day; administrative dissolution after 90 days of non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required only for reporting issuers or entities with public interest status; generally not applicable to private limited partnerships
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP for financial reporting with tax accounting under Income Tax Act

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual ultimate beneficial ownership confirmation required under FINTRAC AML guidelines; partner changes must be notified to registry within 15 business days

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal general corporate rate under Part I of the Income Tax Act, after application of the 13% general tax reduction; the Canadian limited partnership is fiscally transparent and is not a taxpayer, and each corporate partner is taxed on its allocated share of Canadian-source income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No separate LP-level levy. Active business income allocated to a Canadian-controlled private corporation partner is eligible for the Small Business Deduction (9% effective federal rate on the first CA$500,000). Non-resident corporate partners are taxed only on the allocated Canadian-source proportion, and treaty rates may reduce royalty and interest income to 0%-15%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (with Schedules 1, 8, 125, 301 and related schedules); filed electronically through CRA EFILE-approved software (e.g., TaxCycle, Intuit Profile) or the CRA My Business Account portal. The limited partnership must separately file Form T5013 (Partnership Information Return) to report allocations to partners.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Part I tax instalments are payable quarterly where the corporation's unpaid tax balance exceeds CA$3,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return must be filed within six months after the fiscal period-end; the balance of Part I tax is due within two months after year-end for most corporations, and within three months for corporations eligible for the Small Business Deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from webtoon digital subscriptions, chapter-unlocking purchases, and Apple IAP / Google Play Billing sales net of refunds; platform commissions are not netted against gross revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the corporate partner's allocated share of the LP's Canadian-source gross revenue as computed on Schedule 1 of the T5013; do not exclude revenue collected through Apple or Google merely because the payment rail is foreign.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate of gross sales, subscription income, and ancillary syndication or licensing income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Restrict to Canadian-source amounts attributable to the LP business carried on through a permanent establishment in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenditures: content production, localization and translation, server hosting, Apple/Google platform commission, app-store administrative fees, and direct marketing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses wholly applicable to the Canadian-source business and supported by invoices; app-store commissions must be allocated on a reasonable cost basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of partnership net income or loss and the allocation of income among general and limited partners according to the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a T5013 summary showing the non-resident partner's share; the partner must file a T2 (or T1, if applicable) to report the allocation, not merely the cash distributions received.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions and loss carryovers applied; for a non-resident corporation, Canadian taxable income is the allocated partnership income less treaty-eligible deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty relief (e.g., absence of a permanent establishment) is claimed in the T2 return, supported by Form NR301 and a home-country Tax Residency Certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% for each full month late (maximum 12 months); a second late-filing offence within three years raises the penalty to 10% plus 2% per month (maximum 20 months); arrears interest is charged at the prescribed daily compounded rate; cumulative failures may trigger criminal prosecution under s. 239 of the Income Tax Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII statutory rate applies to dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to a non-resident. For the Canadian limited partnership, cash distributions to partners are not dividends; the LP is fiscally transparent and no Part XIII withholding applies to profit distributions. The non-resident corporate partner is instead subject to Part I tax on its allocated share of the LP's Canadian-source income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke reduced treaty rates, the non-resident beneficial owner obtains a Tax Residency Certificate from its residence jurisdiction (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for the United States) and files Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Treaty) with the Canadian payer or withholding agent. Where excessive Part XIII tax was withheld, the non-resident files Form NR7 within two years of the end of the calendar year in which the tax was withheld. For Part I relief claimed on a T2 return, treaty benefits are asserted directly in the return, with the Tax Residency Certificate appended.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII: 25% for both royalties and interest. Under the Canada-US DTA: royalties for copyright of literary or artistic works (webtoon content) are 0%; industrial royalties (platform software, know-how, patents) are 10%; arm's length interest is generally 0%, and interest on participating debt is 15%. Under the Canada-UK DTA: royalties are 10%; interest is generally 0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate arm's length value of reportable non-arm's length cross-border transactions triggers the Local File and Form T106 information return; a Master File is required where the consolidated group revenue exceeds CAD 50,000,000; a Country-by-Country Report is due at group turnover of CAD 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; the CRA instead enforces economic substance through the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR, s. 245 of the Income Tax Act), the reasonable-expectation-of-profit rule, and the anti-hybrid and anti-conduit provisions (ss. 18(4), 94, 95). These jointly require the LP to execute genuine Canadian commercial activity — content production, local licensing, platform management, and active decision-making — to avoid recharacterization as a treaty-shopping shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Apple IAP and Google Play Billing webtoon revenue from the LP's records; falsifying T5013 allocations; creating a fictitious exempt foreign partner; laundering chapter-unlock microtransactions through a foreign shell payment processor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal liability under s. 239(1) of the Income Tax Act: a fine ranging from 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years on indictment; civil reassessment plus a s. 163(2) gross-negligence penalty equal to 50% of the understated tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner are jointly and severally liable under s. 227.1 for unremitted Part I instalments; upon conviction, courts may order restitution, passport seizure, and travel bans through the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act enforcement framework.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Canadian LP as a conduit to route webtoon royalties to a zero-tax foreign partner while all creative and sales functions occur offshore; executing circular financing arrangements with no real Canadian commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR (s. 245) disallows the entirety of the tax benefit; a 25% GAAR penalty applies under s. 163(2.2); the CRA recharacterizes the arrangement and reassesses the non-resident partner directly under Part I, retroactively denying treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certified sham partnership agreements are personally exposed to the 25% GAAR penalty and, for willful participation, prosecution under s. 239; the CRA may obtain a civil court order preventing departure from Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying an inflated royalty to a related foreign IP-holding company for the webtoon platform, or pricing content-licensing fees outside the arm's length range, without contemporaneous Local File, Master File, or Form T106 information return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer-pricing adjustment under s. 247(2) with no correlative relief; a s. 247(3) penalty of 10% of the net upward adjustment applies where the taxpayer fails to make reasonable efforts to price at arm's length or fails to maintain required documentation; a T106 late-filing penalty of CA$100 per day, up to CA$2,500 per failure, is also imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner may be assessed personally for the adjusted tax and penalties as related parties under s. 247 if they signed the transfer-pricing certificates; the CRA may also freeze the LP's merchant payment rails and issue a requirement to pay against director bank accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Part XIII Withholding and Remittance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold 25% Part XIII tax on royalties or interest paid to a non-resident licensor of the webtoon technology; mischaracterizing subscription revenue as non-taxable pass-through to avoid the withholding obligation; late or incomplete remittance of deducted amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 227(8) makes the LP liable for the full unreported withholding plus interest; s. 227(9) imposes a penalty of 10% of the amount that should have been withheld, up to CA$10,000; the non-resident recipient may also be reassessed under Part XIII with a gross-up.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner are absolutely and personally liable under s. 227.1 for the unremitted amounts, regardless of the LP's solvency; the CRA can freeze personal bank accounts, place holds on cross-border payments, and obtain a departure-ban court order until the liability is fully satisfied.
